text: Add a new account by scanning the QR code a service shows, then generate its codes
quote: Open Ente Auth. Tap the add button and scan the QR code shown by the service.

text: Add an account manually by entering the account name, issuer, and secret setup key
quote: Enter the account name, issuer, and secret (setup key).

text: The QR scanner has a scan frame and a torch (flashlight) control
quote: Added a scan frame and torch control to the QR scanner.

text: Import 2FA codes from QR code images on desktop
quote: Added support for importing 2FA codes from QR code images on desktop.

text: Natively imports from 2FAS, Aegis, andOTP, Bitwarden, Google Authenticator, LastPass, Proton, and Raivo OTP
quote:
2FAS Authenticator
*   Aegis Authenticator
*   andOTP (including encrypted backups, except MOTP)
*   Bitwarden
*   Google Authenticator
*   LastPass
*   Proton
*   Raivo OTP

text: Import from unsupported providers by converting their data into Ente's plaintext files first
quote: you might be still able to import from them by first converting the data from your old provider into these plaintext files and then importing those into Ente

text: Migrate Authy codes by generating a file in Ente's plaintext export format and importing it
quote: This will generate a text file called `authy_codes.txt`, which contains your Authy codes in Ente's plaintext export format. You can now import this to Ente Authenticator!

text: Import backups from OTP Auth
quote: Added support for importing backups from OTP Auth

text: Import multi-QR Google Authenticator exports in a single session
quote: Import multi-QR Google Authenticator exports in a single session.

text: Notes are kept when importing Aegis and Bitwarden exports
quote: Preserve notes when importing Aegis and Bitwarden exports.

text: Import Ente Auth's own encrypted exports and plain text files
quote: Ente Auth also supports imports from Auth's own encrypted exports and plain text files.

text: Import an encrypted backup without signing in
quote: Also, exporting the encrypted backup is another good way to reduce the risk (you can easily import the encrypted backup without signing in).

text: Use the app without an account; in offline mode, codes are stored only on that device
quote: Ente Auth can be used without an account by choosing **Use without backups**. In offline mode, your codes are stored only on that device.

text: Automatic daily local backups, created once per day when the app is opened
quote: Automatic daily backups: When enabled, Ente Auth creates one local backup per day when you open the app.

text: Local backups are encrypted with a user-set password that Ente cannot recover
quote: Password-protected: All local backups are encrypted with a password you set. Keep this password safe, because Ente cannot recover it for you.

text: Choose a custom location on the device to store backups
quote: Custom backup location: Choose where to store your backups on your device.

text: Back up Auth codes automatically with Ente's CLI, so backup workflows can be scripted
quote: You can use [Ente's CLI](https://github.com/ente/ente/tree/main/cli#readme) to automatically backup your Auth codes.

text: End-to-end encrypted cloud backups protect against losing tokens
quote: Auth provides end-to-end encrypted cloud backups so you don't have to worry about losing your tokens.

text: Data is encrypted with a key derived from the user's password
quote: the data is encrypted using a key derived from the user's password

text: Encrypted export format is documented, including JSON structure, versioning, and key derivation parameters
quote: The following sections describe the JSON structure, versioning, and key derivation parameters of the encrypted export.

text: Create password-protected encrypted exports of codes
quote: An encrypted Auth export uses a key derived from the password you choose when creating that export.

text: Codes can be exported in Ente's plaintext export format
quote: This will generate a text file called `authy_codes.txt`, which contains your Authy codes in Ente's plaintext export format.

text: Recovery key can bypass Ente account 2FA if you are locked out
quote: We recommend that you ensure you store your recovery key in a safe place (writing it down on a paper is a good idea). This key can be used to bypass Ente 2FA in case you are locked out.

text: Ente account offers Legacy emergency contacts and passkey support
quote: Ente also offers [Legacy](/help/photos/features/legacy/) (emergency contacts) and support for [Passkeys](/help/photos/features/passkeys).

text: Self-host the Ente server and point the Auth apps at it
quote: Alternatively, if using Ente Auth, get started by adding an account (assuming you are running Ente Auth at `http://<machine-ip>:3003` or `http://localhost:3003`).

text: Share specific codes with a team through temporary end-to-end encrypted links
quote: You can now easily share specific codes with your team, with temporary links that are end-to-end encrypted.

text: Sharing works only for TOTP codes; HOTP entries are supported but cannot be shared
quote: Sharing is now limited to TOTP codes; the share option is hidden for HOTP entries.

text: Attach notes of up to 500 characters to accounts
quote: You can attach any text (upto a maximum of 500 characters), to provide more information about your accounts.

text: Move unneeded codes to Trash, then recover them or delete them permanently
quote: You can now trash codes that you don't need. ... You can recover codes from here, in case of accidental deletions, or delete them permanently.

text: Edit or delete a code by long-pressing it, or right-clicking on desktop
quote: You can delete or edit a code by long pressing (or right clicking on desktop) on that item.

text: View and delete codes that could not be parsed
quote: Added a way to view and delete Auth codes that could not be parsed.

text: Custom lock screen protects codes with a PIN or password
quote: You can now further protect your codes with a custom lock screen that supports PINs and passwords.

text: FaceID biometric lock for the app
quote: You can enable FaceID lock under Settings → Security → Lockscreen.

text: Apps for mobile, desktop, and web, with codes synced across devices end-to-end encrypted
quote: Auth has an app for every platform. Mobile, desktop and web. Your codes sync across all your devices, end-to-end encrypted.

text: Available on Flathub for Linux desktop
quote: Auth is now officially available on [Flathub](https://flathub.org/apps/io.ente.auth)!

text: Optional macOS menu bar mode for quick access to codes
quote: Added an optional menu bar mode on macOS for quick access to your 2FA codes (@ivnnv).

text: Type-to-search on desktop for faster code lookup
quote: Added type-to-search on desktop for faster code lookup (@StDensity).

text: Search deep links via the enteauth://search URL scheme
quote: Added support for search deep links via enteauth://search.

text: Show the next upcoming code ahead of time
quote: Save time by viewing your next code

text: Service icons make tokens easy to identify
quote: Easily identify your tokens by their icons

text: Pin favorite services to the top of the list
quote: Favorite services to the top

text: Tags organize codes; tag strips scroll with mouse or drag and are keyboard-navigable
quote: Tag strips that overflow can now be scrolled with the mouse wheel or by dragging, and tag chips are reachable with Tab and selectable with Enter or Space.
